Subject: Throughput fingerprint & SLO gamma analysis — OrionMed pilot

Aisha / Marco,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. To keep momentum for the pilot, can we align on a short throughput/latency fingerprint so Redwood can size a dedicated pool for the initial 3-month pilot? Specifically, we need:

- Typical request shape (prompt tokens vs generated tokens)
- Peak concurrent requests you expect during clinic hours (approx windows + scale factor)
- Target SLOs (p50/p95 latency targets) and acceptable degradation modes (e.g., degrade to smaller model or lower context)

If you can share a quick sample (or tell us the average prompt/generation token counts), I’ll run a tokens/sec -> GPU mapping and propose a safety matrix. I’ve attached a worksheet template that we can populate together (orionmed-throughput-fingerprint-v1.xlsx).

Proposed next step: 30m workshop Thursday to validate numbers and confirm model variant. Are you available 8/5 10-10:30am PT?

Best,
Jordan Blake

Jordan —

Thanks, attached is a filled form (summary below). Happy to take the 8/5 slot.

Quick summary (pilot scope):
- Workload: Clinical note summarization and triage helper (short prompts, structured JSON output)
- Average prompt tokens: 280 tokens
- Average generated tokens: 420 tokens
- Expected peak concurrent requests during clinic windows (9am-5pm ET): 28 concurrent users, expected burst up to 60 concurrent requests for 2-3 minutes when rounds start
- Target latency SLO: p50 < 220ms, p95 < 420ms (end-to-end for generation for our web UI); acceptable fallback: route to smaller model with degraded context if p95 breaches 700ms
- Security/compliance: SOC2 in progress; procurement will need audit log detail

Attached: completed spreadsheet and our SLO doc.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Khan <akhan@orionmed.com>, Marco Ribeiro <marco.r@orionmed.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 5 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput fingerprint & SLO gamma analysis — OrionMed pilot

Aisha / Marco — thanks for the detail and the attachments. I ran the numbers from your spreadsheet and sketched a conservative mapping. Highlights below (I'll bring a one-page handoff to the workshop):

Summary of expected token flow (pilot baseline):
- Avg tokens per request = prompt (280) + gen (420) = 700 tokens
- Pilot baseline concurrent steady-state: 28 requests -> aggregate TPS estimate = (28 requests * 700 tokens) / avg_time_window; but we model at tokens/sec per GPU for direct mapping.

Redwood runtime assumptions used:
- Model: open-llm-curie-8k (float16) baseline, with option to fall back to open-llm-mini (8-bit quant) at high load
- Measured tokens/sec per A100-40GB equivalent (conservative) = 55 tokens/sec for curie-8k at typical prompt shape and 1-stream concurrency. With batching and continuous packing we can push effective tokens/sec per GPU to ~180 tokens/sec at moderate latency tradeoff.

Sizing proposal (pilot dedicated pool):
- Baseline desired capacity (no burst): to meet p50/p95 targets comfortably we need ~3 GPUs (A100-equivalent) mapped as:
  - 1x serving slab optimized for p50-critical low-latency traffic (limited batching, 55 tokens/sec raw)
  - 2x throughput slabs allowing higher batching/packing (effective 160-180 tokens/sec each)
- This maps to an expected steady effective capacity of ~375 tokens/sec (2*180 + 55). With 700 tokens per request that maps to ~0.53 requests/sec steady (~32 requests/min), which covers the 28 concurrent steady users with modest interleaving and gives a small steady cushion.

Burst and safety margin:
- For short bursts to 60 concurrent we model an up to 2.0x temporary multiplier on request rate. To maintain p95<420ms during 2-3 minute bursts we recommend enabling:
  1) short-term burst pool (on-demand from cloud) sized to +3 GPUs for first 10 minutes of a burst, and
  2) automatic fallback policy to open-llm-mini (8-bit) beyond sustained burst thresholds to preserve service availability.
- Proposed safety margin: 30% across the mapping for unexpected token length variance and quantization performance delta. This yields an operational target of ~490 tokens/sec headroom needed during peak planning.

Estimated latency fit (empirical):
- p50: ~180-240ms on the p50-optimized slab for typical requests
- p95: ~380-520ms variable depending on batching at the time (we tune to hit your 420ms target by adjusting split between low-latency and throughput slabs)

Operational asks / next steps for workshop:
- Confirm whether the model must be deterministic (affects quantization choices)
- Confirm allowed fallback model list and any data residency constraints for burst pool
- Procurement folks to confirm contract cadence for burst hours and SLA credits

I'll present a 10-minute walk-through of the worksheet and a proposed canary plan (1 GPU for 48h traffic replay) on the call.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks for the clear sizing and safety options. Procurement reviewed the rough numbers and they are comfortable with the +3 GPU burst approach if we can limit burst billing to discrete windows and include a 2-week audit of usage after pilot ramp.

We are ok to proceed with the proposed 3 GPU baseline + burst plan. Please send over the canary schedule and a short contract appendix that covers:
- burst billing windows and caps
- rollback clause if p95 consistently breaches 700ms for >10 minutes
- required audit logs (request id-level token counts)

I'll coordinate with procurement on the HubSpot deal and sign the pilot SOW once we have the appendix. Looking forward to the 8/5 workshop and the canary.

Marco Ribeiro
